discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

motivation: Zoller and co-workers showed in 1998 that ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Bose-Hubbard model, turning light-shifted atoms into a controllable quantum simulator. In 2002 Greiner and Bloch observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition, the first quantum phase transition engineered with atoms. Greiner and Bloch then invented quantum gas microscopes, imaging and controlling strongly correlated matter atom by atom: antiferromagnetic order in the Fermi-Hubbard model, many-body localisation, entanglement entropy and string order. This programme, a model of theory closely guiding experiment, created the field of analog quantum simulation and supplied tools now ubiquitous across physics, including the lattice platforms underpinning optical clocks, ultracold molecule experiments and neutral-atom quantum processors. It answers questions in condensed matter physics that classical computation cannot, and it has transformed atomic physics from precision spectroscopy of single particles into the controlled study of quantum many-body systems.
